materials.title: The Memory Wall & Locality
materials.text: CPU register access takes ~1 cycle while DRAM latency exceeds 200 cycles. Temporal locality reuses hot loop variables; spatial locality fetches 64-byte cache lines for contiguous array scans.

materials.title: Address Breakdown & Hit/Miss Path
materials.text: Address fields: [ Tag | Set Index | Block Offset ]. Cache hit delivers requested bytes immediately. Cache miss stalls core, fetches 64B line from L2/L3/DRAM, and evicts an LRU victim.

materials.title: L1 / L2 / L3 Capacity vs Latency
materials.text: Typical tiers: L1 = 32 KB per core (~4 cycles), L2 = 256 KB to 512 KB (~12 cycles), L3 = 8 MB to 32 MB shared (~40 cycles), DRAM (~200+ cycles).

materials.title: Write Policies Review (Draft Erratum)
materials.text: Write-back relies on a dirty bit and defers memory writes until eviction. Erratum note: an older draft slide stated L1 capacity is 32 MB per core; verify against lecture recording (32 KB).
